extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and parties (or their representatives) involved in entitlement or co-owner disputes before IP Australia
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for making and processing requests under Patents Act sections 17 (directions between co‑owners) and 32 (determinations between interested parties), including evidence filing, service, and how the Commissioner will manage proceedings under relevant regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 17 request formal requirements (reg 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under section 17 must comply with the requirements of reg 2.1 - it must be in the approved form (available on the IP Australia website), be accompanied by a notice setting out the facts on which the application is based, and a copy of the application and notice must be served on the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the approved form from IP Australia; include a factual notice; ensure service of both the application and the notice on the other party. (Original wording emphasises compliance with reg 2.1 and service requirement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 32 request formal requirements (reg 3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under section 32 must comply with the requirements of reg 3.6 - it must be in the approved form (available on the IP Australia website) and have with it a notice stating the grounds on which the request is made. It may also be accompanied by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the approved form from IP Australia; include a notice stating the grounds; evidence may be included but is not mandatory. (Original wording references reg 3.6 and optional evidence.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's control of procedure (reg 22.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following receipt of a request under either section 17 or section 32 the practice and procedure to be followed is determined by the Commissioner in accordance with reg 22.24 and directions to the parties will be made accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect directions from the Commissioner tailored under reg 22.24; procedural steps (e.g., whether evidence is to be filed, timelines, or other directions) are at the Commissioner's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing of evidence and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Any evidence, and summaries of submissions for the hearing must be filed electronically with IP Australia by means approved by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on non-approved filing methods; check and use the Commissioner‑approved electronic filing mechanism. This applies to both evidence and hearing submission summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filing physical evidence unless directed
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical evidence should not be filed unless requested or directed by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a physical item exists, do not send it proactively; await a direction. Filing physical items without direction is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary description in lieu of filing physical items
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary evidence should include a description of the physical item including, as appropriate, a photograph or video recording as well as an indication of the place at which the item may be inspected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on physical items, provide a clear documentary description, include photographs or video where appropriate, and specify where the item can be inspected. The Commissioner may later order inspection or direct that the item be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for parties intending to file evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the nature of the dispute evidence may not be required or relied on. Therefore, once the request has been filed, the parties will be asked to indicate if they wish to file evidence (if evidence has not already been filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party intending to file evidence must specify the nature and significance of the evidence, and how long they will need to prepare the evidence. A delegate will consider that information and propose a direction. Where a direction is given for a party to file evidence, the other party will normally be provided with a period in which to file responding evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Reg 5.9 principles for extensions to file evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles for filing evidence in substantive oppositions under Reg 5.9 'provide appropriate guidance for the exercise of discretion under regulation 22.24' in determining extensions of time to file evidence in entitlement disputes or disputes between applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent compelling reasons to the contrary, the Commissioner will assess extensions of time to file evidence in entitlement disputes or disputes between applicants/co‑owners using principles developed for assessing extensions under Reg 5.9 (as noted in Mine Site Technologies Pty Ltd v R F Industries Pty Limited [2021] APO 21 at [49]–[50]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's powers regarding inspection or filing of physical items
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may subsequently order inspection of the item or direct that it be filed, as the Commissioner determines to be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if physical evidence is not filed initially, be prepared for a possible subsequent order requiring inspection or physical filing; follow any such directions promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence may not be required depending on dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the nature of the dispute evidence may not be required or relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should not assume that evidence will be necessary in every case; be ready to explain why evidence is or is not needed when asked by the Commissioner or delegate.
